title.narrative: Design of Market Based Emissions Trading Scheme to Improve Air Quality in India

description.narrative: Although no new regulations are required to enable legislative powers to establish the emissions trading scheme, the MOEF will have to issue a notification stating the regulatory authority for emissions trading, the purpose for introducing an emissions trading scheme for particulate matter less than 10 micrometers, the applicability of such a scheme by sector and area, and the broad powers that enable State Pollution Control Boards (SPCB) to implement, monitor and evaluate the scheme. The state governments and State Pollution Control Boards (SPCB) may then institute the recommended emissions norms for PM10 and permit requirements in their place by revising the terms of industrial consents to establish and operate for participating firms. During this component, it will be critical to consult widely with stakeholders, in particular the targeted regulated communities, to ensure seek their inputs on the design of the emissions trading scheme, and to secure their buy-in. Successfully reaching an agreement with the industry associations is an essential premise to move forward, and the parameters that are critical to address in the design include: (i) setting the target for aggregate emissions for PM 10 from the sector where trading is introduced, which is to be set at a level to produce reasonable prices and emission reductions (ii) allocating permits, which must be distributed in an equitable way to build support for the scheme (iii) the regulatory framework must make industries confident that buying permits is the only reliable way to meet the environmental obligations. Outcome The basic structure of the emissions trading scheme is established, a notification is issued by the MOEF on emissions trading for PM10, and institutional arrangements are in place to oversee the implementation and piloting phase. This component will be conducted during the first year (Apr. 2011- Dec. 2011). Interim steps towards this component include the solicitation of public comments on the draft notification. (i) to build the capacity of environmental regulators with the use of economic instruments, and (ii) to design an emissions trading scheme for suspended particulate matter, that will introduce continuous monitoring and transparency and enable cost effective compliance of air quality standards in India. To begin with the emissions trading scheme is intending to target around 900 polluting industries which emit particulate matter (PM10) in 3 states.
